results.question: When did the Great Library of Alexandria burn, and who is traditionally blamed?
results.reference: No single burning destroyed it; decline spanned centuries. Julius Caesar's 48 BCE fire is the traditional story but scholars dispute that it destroyed the main collection; the Mouseion institution faded by the 3rd century CE.

results.question: Which chemical element has the highest melting point, and what is it in degrees Celsius?
results.reference: Tungsten (W), 3422 C. Carbon sublimes rather than melting at atmospheric pressure, so tungsten holds the record.
results.answer:
[1] Tungsten — Properties
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all known elements, 3422 °C. Carbon sublimes rather than melting at atmospheric pressure, so tungsten holds the melting-point record among metals and all elements that melt.

results.question: Who won the women's singles title at Wimbledon in 1977?
results.reference: Virginia Wade, defeating Betty Stove in the final. It was the centenary Wimbledon and the Silver Jubilee year.
results.answer:
[1] 1977 Wimbledon Championships
The 1977 Wimbledon Championships was a tennis tournament played on outdoor grass courts. Virginia Wade defeated Betty Stove in the women's singles final. It was the centenary Wimbledon, held in the year of the Queen's Silver Jubilee.

results.question: The Eiffel Tower was originally built under a 20-year concession. When did it expire, and why was the tower not demolished?
results.reference: Concession expired 1909. Kept because Gustave Eiffel had installed scientific instruments and, decisively, a radio antenna; its military communications value saved it.
results.answer:
[1] Eiffel Tower — Survival
The tower was built under a 20-year concession that expired in 1909. It was spared from demolition because Gustave Eiffel had installed scientific instruments on it and, decisively, a radio antenna whose military communications value proved indispensable.

results.question: What does the 'S' stand for in Harry S. Truman's name?
results.reference: Nothing. It is not an initial for a name; it honors both of his grandfathers, Anderson Shipp Truman and Solomon Young. Truman himself said the S should not have a period, though convention adds one.
results.answer:
[1] Harry S. Truman — The middle initial
The "S" in Truman's name does not stand for anything. It was chosen to honor both of his grandfathers, Anderson Shipp Truman and Solomon Young. Truman himself noted that the S should not be followed by a period, though convention usually adds one.
